Branches and the preview link

The old staging link keeps showing exactly what it shows today until you approve the merge.

feat/leapswitch-staging→ cutleapswitch-redesign
↳ task branches (feat/shell-nav, feat/mf-overview …) with a PR intoleapswitch-redesign
leapswitch-redesign→ test everything onls-redesign.unifolio.in
then staging merged in, fast-forward only →feat/leapswitch-staging→ deploy →ls-staging.unifolio.in
  • Both links call the same API, database, worker and cron jobs.
  • Backend changes are additive only, so the old link and the mobile app are unchanged.
  • Testers sign in separately on each link (separate browser storage).

Merge-back safety

The merged staging branch is the exact tree you tested.

  • Merge staging into the redesign branch first; the final merge is fast-forward only.
  • Full backend and frontend suites on that merged tree.
  • Old branch's backend tests run against the migrated database.
  • Same synthetic CAS statements on both links; every shared number must match.
  • Mobile smoke test on both links; rollback tag pre-redesign-staging.

Steps only you can do

  • Route 53: A record ls-redesign.unifolio.in → the VM's IP.
  • Google console: add the new origin for Google sign-in.
  • On the VM: worktree, shared .env lines, first deploy command.
  • Relay each Codex review result (/codex:status, /codex:result).
  • Push task branches and merge PRs into leapswitch-redesign when ready.
  • Browser QA on the preview link; final PR and the production-style deploy.

Full list with commands: Docs/orchestration/2026-10-24-ui-redesign-manual-steps.md

Decisions already taken

  • Sidebar active row uses the green underline; Profile uses plan defaults.
  • Home uses stored prices and adds no new table; its staging measurement is done.
  • News is shown directly (GDELT only).
  • Fund logos reuse the old review screen's source, initials as fallback.
  • Individual Fund page: Overview, Overlap, Insights; comparison is a second state, no URL.
  • Benchmark windows 1Y / 3Y / 5Y / Since inception, stored beside the old payload.
  • A fund name opens the individual fund page wherever a page lists funds; the old fund popup is retired.
  • Each page keeps the surface style of its own mockup; the mockup sidebar and top bar are ignored (the shell draws them).
  • Investments and Mutual Funds mockups are light only: dark is derived from the palette and checked at parity.

Biggest risks, and the guard

  • New indices change old output → old code paths keep a legacy four-index tuple, tested.
  • Recompute gets slower → one index load per index, a timing gate before merge.
  • compute_holdings is shared → one owner (Home T1), Opus review.
  • Wrong checkout on the VM → pinned compose project, absolute bundle paths, script guards.

Run counts for planned items come from each plan's own run table or from batching two to three tasks per run. Waves 5 to 7 are estimates; Wave 6 is open-ended and depends on QA findings.

The app after all 88 runs

Every page of the redesigned desktop app inside one 1440 px window, built from the signed-off mockups (not redrawn). The left panel and top bar come from the shell contract; each page is its own live mockup, so tabs, periods, states, popups and rows respond. Use Light and Dark at the top right. Sample data only.

What this shows, and what to keep in mind

The finished app. Every page as in its signed-off mockup, with the shell's sidebar and top bar around it. Links work as planned: the tab strip inside Mutual Funds switches tabs; a fund row in the Overview table opens the individual fund page; the Overview table shows Today's change and its headers sort; Home's fund and concentration links open the fund page and Fund Overlap; "View in Analytics" opens Allocation; the search box opens the Mira popup.
Individual fund page. Three tabs: Overview and Insights (individual-fund plans) and Overlap Analysis (Mutual Funds plan, with its comparison state).
Surface styles. Each page keeps the style of its own mockup: Home, Planning, Profile and the individual fund use palette grey cards on a near-white page; Investments and the seven Mutual Funds tabs use white cards on a grey page. You see that change when you move between pages.
Dark mode. Home, Planning, Profile and the individual fund have a designed dark theme. Investments and the Mutual Funds tabs were drawn light only; their dark view here is derived from the palette's dark values and is checked in each page's parity step.
Today's change. The Mutual Funds Overview fund table has a Today's change column and sortable headers (decided). Home's "View all by day's change" opens that table sorted; the news "See affected holdings" opens it unsorted.
Smaller notes. Fund logos are initials here; the real app loads fund-house logos with initials as the fallback. All data is sample data and each page uses its own invented funds.
